config.title: Build typed retry policy config

intro.title: Build typed retry policy config
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed configuration object for a retry policy, which defines rules like how many times an operation should retry and how long to wait between attempts. You will learn to use TypeScript's type system to ensure this configuration is always valid and correctly structured. The main constructs involved are TypeScript interfaces and optional properties. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe configuration that can be used in functions that handle retrying failed operations.
intro.usecase: Typed retry policies are essential in production-grade applications that handle unreliable network connections or external API dependencies. You'll see this pattern in dashboard applications that fetch live data from multiple sources, where failed requests need automatic retries with configurable delays and limits. Payment processing systems use typed retry configurations to safely retry failed transactions with exponential backoff strategies. Form submissions in enterprise applications often implement retry logic with typed policies to ensure data persistence even during intermittent connectivity issues.

objectives: Implement a TypeScript interface to define a retry policy configuration
Construct a function that validates retry policy parameters against type constraints
Apply type annotations to enforce limits on retry attempts and delay intervals
Configure a retry policy object with typed properties for maximum attempts and backoff strategy
Manipulate policy settings using TypeScript's type system to ensure runtime safety
Initialize a default retry configuration with proper type definitions
Integrate the typed retry policy into a simulated API call function
